regions.full_page: God bless you and yours. I hope you are well. I hope you are at least resigned to the cross or crosses that the Dear Lord entrusts to your weakness, your poverty . In regard to those thoughtless associates who refer to the "age of miracles" as past; I would say simply that to doubt the truth of miracles in any age of history of seriously to question their existence, would be nothing less than just to fall in line with the ideals of the unbelieving world - deaf, dumb and spiritually blind, - whose WANT of principle is atheism the climax of insanity and whose prince and inspiration is Lucifer himself the king of all (dam) fools. I have two holy Masses this morning - 9 and 12 - and therefore, I can not think of going into details as I would like to do; but just to encourage you to persevere is patience and resignation to God's holy will, I am going to give you a few lines from a Letter received last March, which I happened to pick up and reread just before opening yours of the-day-before yesterday. It comes from a nurse-friend in the State Hospital, Cleveland, Ohio. Here follows some of the letter: ". ... You will remember last August when I was in Detroit how very hectic things were at the hospital. I tried to remem- ber everything religious and beautiful I was ever taught: I tried to think how the Saints prayed for crosses and sufferings; and decided (rightly), it was myself that needed adjusting.
